children: Short sellers have shifted their Treasury ETF positioning toward intermediate maturities ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy decision, even as investors take profits on bets against long-duration debt, according to S3 Research.

TLT, the 20-plus-year Treasury ETF, has been the most profitable short among the four Treasury ETFs tracked by S3. Its price was down 7% this year and 10% over the past 12 months, generating $561M in mark-to-market gains for short sellers year to date, most of the $706M earned across the four funds, S3 said.

Short interest in TLT fell sharply during the spring. From December through the end of April, short sellers covered 60M shares, reducing the position by 40% to 91M shares, or about $7.8B. The position has since remained around 90M to 100M shares, according to S3.

More recently, short positioning has moved toward the belly of the Treasury curve. Since June, short interest in IEF, the 7-to-10-year Treasury ETF, has increased 52% in shares, while short interest in IEI, the 3-to-7-year ETF, has doubled. Together, the 3-to-10-year funds now account for 20% of the four-fund short book, up from 14%, S3 said.

Both IEF and IEI short positions have eased from their August highs, although IEI short interest has started rising again this month. S3 said the recent positioning provides a view of duration hedging through Treasury ETFs used by generalist managers, rather than activity in Treasury futures and cash markets.

Total short interest across the four Treasury ETFs stood at $11.8B, with about two-thirds concentrated in TLT. S3 said TLT had remained the core short for roughly a year, while new hedging activity this summer shifted toward the 3-to-10-year maturities.

S3 said short sellers entered the year betting that persistent inflation, heavy Treasury supply, and a higher term premium would keep long-term yields elevated. Much of that TLT position has since been covered at a profit, while the summer shift toward intermediate maturities reflected greater sensitivity to expectations for the Fed's policy path.

Those intermediate-duration shorts were built through July and into mid-August, before the Jackson Hole meeting and last week's inflation report pushed market expectations for a rate hike toward 90%, according to S3. With a hike now priced by markets, S3 said short sellers were taking profits on long-duration positions while rebuilding some of their intermediate-maturity hedge.

title: Treasury ETF shorts shift toward belly ahead of Fed decision
